It is recognized that criteria provided in the proposed legislation do not spell precisely which species fall under terms of the definitions. Purpose of the action is not only to protect and restore not only those species that now are critically threatened with extinction but to head off the ultimate plight of species that will soon reach the same point even though they are not rare now. It must be recognized that criteria for endangerment must include more than population levels. A given population may be threatened depending upon (1) what the species is or which toxonomic level is involved, (2) how may separate populations be involved; (3) present population trends; and (4) the nature of the threat that is responsible for the condition that exists, among other things. In lieu of more stringent, but impractical, criteria, the proposed legislation, as well as current authority, provides guarantees that proposed listings or changes in listing will be discussed with the States or other Federal agencies involved.
Revocation of Licenses. There was State concern expressed over the provision in the proposed legislation to include suspension of Federal hunting or fishing permit among the penalties for violation of the Act. H.R. 4758, Section 6(a)(3) reads, in part, "The Secretary shall also suspend for a period of up to one year; or cancel any Federal hunting or fishing permits or stamps issued to any person who is convicted of a criminal violation of this Act or any regulation or permit issued hereunder."
